strategyPosture: Stay selective and staged. Credit is loose (SLOOS 0%, HY OAS 3.09%) and the index is near its high, so there is no confirmed rollover to de-risk against — but a 5.61% 30-year and rotating leadership argue for owning the verified dislocations (AVGO-grade fundamentals at sentiment prices) rather than chasing the nuclear unwind or paying up at the index level.

themes.counterRead: Historically this combination — index near highs, leadership diverging, credit loose — resolves as rotation rather than a confirmed broad top. But the divergence is real: if the gap widens while credit starts confirming, the read flips. Position for churn in leadership, not for index collapse.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 names average 10.14% below their 52-week highs versus SPY at 1% — a 9.14-point divergence gap. TSLA is the weakest Mag7 name at 24.8% off its high; AAPL the strongest at 1.4%. Bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 0%, far below the ~40% stress threshold) and HY OAS sits at 3.09% — credit is not confirming a rollover. VIX at 15.16, down 15.02% over one month, agrees with rotation rather than stress.
themes.label: Rotation, Not Rollover
themes.narrative: The index looks calm — SPY at $777.05, only 1% below its 52-week high and essentially flat on the day (−0.02%) — so the market read is that nothing is wrong. Underneath, leadership is rotating: QQQ fell 0.54% on the day while IWM rose 0.32%, and the names that carried the index are well off their own highs.
themes.watchFor: Divergence gap: narrowing from 9.14 pts means rotation healing; widening past ~12 pts with HY OAS above 3.50% means rollover risk.

themes.counterRead: The speculative leg (SMR, OKLO) has no fundamental anchor in the current data — those declines are sentiment-driven and can extend. BWXT is the opposite shape: a real business being sold with the theme. Lumping them together is the error; the unwind is narrative-ahead for the story stocks and data-ahead for the quality name.
themes.dataAnchor: The month's laggards are dominated by nuclear: SMR −31.45% in one month (−3.39% today), OKLO −17.43% (−4.54% today), URA −16.56% (−2.08% today), CCJ −11.91%. The complex is not homogeneous — BWXT is 41.2% below its high while revenue grows 18.3% YoY with positive FCF ($185M), a divergence the screen scores 77 (Tier B). VST itself is 28.1% below its high on a PARTIAL_SIGNAL sentiment-driven tag with a still-positive +3.3% one-month trend.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI Power Unwind
themes.narrative: The AI-power complex is still being unwound as a crowded narrative trade: the market is treating every nuclear name as the same story stock and selling the complex together, with holding VST down 4.81% today.
themes.watchFor: SMR/OKLO posting two consecutive positive weeks after −31.45%/−17.43% months would mark capitulation ending; BWXT reclaiming a positive 1-month trend on its revenue base is the quality tell.

themes.counterRead: Fundamentals and price are moving in opposite directions — that is the definition of the setup, but it is not a timing signal by itself. A 5.61% 30-year caps the multiple the market will pay for even this growth, so the discount can persist until the rate path or the next print forces a re-rate.
themes.dataAnchor: AVGO is the screen's top conviction name (score 81, Tier A): revenue growing 55% YoY, gross margin 67.8%, free cash flow $26,914M at a 42.1% FCF margin — while the stock sits at $360.14, 27.2% below its 52-week high, RSI 49.3, tagged FULL_SIGNAL with a SENTIMENT_DRIVEN decline reason. The semi-equipment layer underneath confirms recovery rather than rollover: AMAT +8.7% and KLAC +7.6% one-month trends on MULTIPLE_COMPRESSION decline tags, CLS revenue +28.5% YoY, VRT revenue +27.7% YoY.
themes.label: AI Infrastructure Quality at a Discount
themes.narrative: The tape is pricing Broadcom like a cyclical that already peaked — sold off with the AI complex on a sentiment-driven decline signal despite no fundamental break in the data.
themes.watchFor: AVGO holding above its recent range low while revenue growth stays near +55% YoY at the next print; a revenue deceleration would close the fundamentals-ahead-of-price gap from the wrong side.

themes.counterRead: Tight credit plus a steep curve is a multiple-compression regime, not a recession signal — it punishes long-duration cash flows (small caps, unprofitable growth) while cash-generative quality holds up. The risk is a hot CPI on Oct 14 pushing the 30-year through 5.61% and turning compression into a broader de-rating.
themes.dataAnchor: The curve has bear-steepened: DGS2 4.77%, DGS10 5.23%, DGS30 5.61%, 2s10s +0.46, real 10-year 2.88%, breakeven (T10YIE) 2.35%. HY OAS at 3.09% says credit disagrees with the stress story. The casualty is duration-sensitive breadth: IWM is −4.15% over one month and −5.08% over three while SPY is +1.92%/+4.25% and QQQ +5.21%/+5.93%. Fed funds (DFF) sit at 3.88% with FOMC decisions on Oct 27–28 and Dec 8–9 ahead.
themes.label: The Long End Is the Pressure Point
themes.narrative: The market's anxiety is inflation and duration — event headlines flag 'inflation jitters' into the September CPI on Oct 14 — not credit or growth collapse.
themes.watchFor: September CPI on Oct 14: DGS30 holding at or below 5.61% keeps the compression contained; a push through 5.75% with HY OAS widening past 3.50% changes the regime.

themes.counterRead: Depth of drawdown is not evidence of value — some of these declines are the market correctly repricing slower futures, and the screen does not separate those from sentiment overshoot. This is a research queue, not a buy list: each name needs its thesis verified before sizing, exactly as the posture flag in the data states.
themes.dataAnchor: The dislocation screen flags FULL_SIGNAL sentiment-driven declines in names whose revenue still grows: NOW is 27.6% below its high with revenue +23.1% YoY (score 70, RSI 56.4); HUBS is 53.4% below its high; APP is 62% below its high with 76% gross margin and $3,480M FCF at a 60.8% margin (score 76, Tier B); KTOS is 68.7% below its high with revenue +26.9% YoY and RSI 32.9; NXT is 47.7% below its high with revenue +20.3% YoY. The pullback posture in the data is RESEARCH_SCREENED — every candidate passed the 5-gate screen, but the screen verifies dislocation, not thesis.
themes.label: Dislocated Quality Growth
themes.narrative: A broad set of former growth leaders has been written off as broken — software and platform names sit 25–70% below their highs and the market is pricing them as structurally impaired.
themes.watchFor: Names from this screen printing revenue re-acceleration on their next reports while holding above post-decline bases; continued estimate cuts on the same names would confirm the impairment read instead.

watchFor: September CPI on Oct 14 — DGS30 (now 5.61%) holding at or below 5.61% vs pushing through 5.75%
Mag7-vs-SPY 52-week-high divergence gap narrowing from 9.14 pts (rotation healing) or widening past ~12 pts (rollover risk)
HY OAS staying at or below ~3.25% (credit calm) vs breaking above 3.50% (credit confirming stress)
AVGO holding its recent range while revenue growth prints near +55% YoY — the data-ahead test case
SMR/OKLO two consecutive positive weeks after −31.45%/−17.43% months — capitulation signal for the nuclear complex
whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds on the rate path into September CPI (Oct 14) and the Oct 27–28 FOMC: a soft print relieves the long end and re-rates the dislocated quality growth first; a hot print extends multiple compression, with IWM (−5.08% over three months) as the pressure gauge.
